articles.title: JJ Redick Talks Lakers' 'Silly Fine' System, Reveals Luka Has Won Prize Money the Most 'By Far'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed Wednesday night that he has instituted a unique way for players to compete for prize money accumulated via fines.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed Wednesday night that he has instituted a unique way for players to compete for prize money accumulated via fines.

Speaking to reporters after the Lakers opened their season with a 127-105 home win over the Golden State Warriors (beginning at the 17:19 mark of the video) , Redick provided some insight into the competition that allows players to vie for fine money he has collected:

"We have a silly fine system, so if you're a minute late to film, you're two minutes late to the bus, $500 [of] your personal cash goes in that pot," Redick said. "We shoot for it every shootaround, and I think by far Luka [Dončić] has won the most."

The conversation came up while discussing the half-court shot Dončić made going into halftime, which extended the Lakers' lead to 66-52.

That accounted for three of Dončić's game-high 28 points in Wednesday's game, which saw Los Angeles carry a 34-point lead into the fourth quarter.

The Warriors made the score look a bit better in the fourth quarter, but it was a one-sided game that the Lakers blew open in the second and third quarters.

Playing their first regular-season game in the post-LeBron James era, the new-look Lakers did not appear to miss a beat.

Dončić, Austin Reaves and offseason acquisition Walker Kessler all scored over 20 points, and five Lakers scored in double figures overall in the victory.

The Lakers will be back in action Friday when they host the rival Los Angeles Clippers at Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: Lakers' Austin Reaves Reveals What He Misses Most About LeBron James After Star's Exit for 76ers
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers will obviously miss LeBron James' skills on the court after he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers. For Austin Reaves, there are more imperceptible ways in which James' absence will be felt.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers will obviously miss LeBron James' skills on the court after he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers. For Austin Reaves, there are more imperceptible ways in which James' absence will be felt.

"I never disregarded the basketball player he was when I was younger," Reaves told ESPN's Ramona Shelburne . "I knew he was great, but then to full-circle being on the team with him, and then him giving me confidence every single day was incredible. It gave me a better outlook on judging people because he treated me the same from the day he met me when I was a two-way player, to when I call him right now. I think that's what I miss the most."

Reaves added that "getting to know him as a human was one of the coolest things I've been able to experience."

Calling James a mentor for Reaves would probably be a stretch because LeBron's ultimate focus during their time together was on winning another title.

But there's the famous clip of an interaction between the two in 2022, when James is giving pointers to a seemingly bemused Reaves. If LeBron saw an opportunity to impart some wisdom on one of his younger teammates, he was going to take it.

There's also the impact a player of his stature can have simply from leading by example. By watching the future Hall of Famer on a daily basis, you'll inevitably start to mimic some of his habits.

Reaves is now a star in his own right. He averaged 23.3 points and 5.5 assists last season before signing a $184.8 million contract to return to the Lakers.

At 28, he's basically the grizzled vet with valuable insight to provide for teammates trying to find their place in the NBA.

In that sense, James' influence in Los Angeles will extend well beyond his tenure there.

articles.title: Draymond Green Explains Why Lakers' Luka Doncic 'Will Never Win an MVP in the NBA'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Draymond Green questioned whether Luka Dončić, a perennial MVP candidate, will ever get over the hump and earn the award.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Draymond Green questioned whether Luka Dončić, a perennial MVP candidate, will ever get over the hump and earn the award.

"Luka will never win an MVP in the NBA. This is the last possible year he can win it," Green said on Wednesday's episode of his podcast (via HoopsHype ). "Because if Luka could go average 34 points a game, they're going to be like, 'Oh, yeah, of course Luka averaged 34 points a game.' And it's like [Jayson Tatum] could go average 30, they're going to be like, 'Oh, yeah, we know he can average 30 points a game.' He can average both of them can average 30, 11, and eight.

Bold Predictions for 2026-27 NBA Season 🔮

"'Oh, yeah, we know they're supposed (to).' It won't be viewed as somebody else averaging those numbers. It it's like people get fatigued of it. Same thing happened with LeBron James. You can't tell me he only should have four MVPs."

Green seems to be making two separate arguments.

Voter fatigue can be a factor with somebody like LeBron James. James' last MVP win was in 2012-13, and you could almost certainly point to some years since then when he was the NBA's single most valuable player.

Michael Jordan winning five MVPs in 15 seasons is cited as another example of this.

But it's a little harder to argue that voters effectively punish consistency over an extended period of time when the Oklahoma City Thunder's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is the two-time reigning MVP. Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokić also received three MVPs over a four-year span and was the runner-up in 2022-23, 2024-25 and 2025-26.

As perhaps a better example, Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid was in his age-28 season and coming off back-to-back runner-up finishes when he was finally crowned MVP in 2022-23. Voters didn't take his monster season for granted because he had maintained a similar level before.

In the case of Dončić specifically, the fact he became an MVP contender in his second season in the NBA isn't why the trophy remains a glaring omission on his résumé.

The six-time All-Star has logged 70-plus appearances just twice in his career, and availability is something to consider within the context of measuring a player's value.

The Dallas Mavericks also had only one top-four finish in the Western Conference during Dončić's first six full seasons there. That kind of team performance will always present a hurdle in an MVP quest.

There's no set criteria for judging the most deserving MVP, but "most valuable" doesn't automatically equate to the best player or the one putting up the best numbers.

It will be surprising if Dončić doesn't have an MVP to show from his career, but there are a lot of distinguished stars from any given era who, for one reason or another, didn't get to enjoy that status, either.

articles.title: Warriors Rookie Follows Up Trash Talk With Shot at Luka Doncic
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had some words for Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic after Wednesday's season opener. The post Warriors R...
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had some words for Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic after the Lakers won their series opener Wednesday, 127-105.

Lendeborg guarded Doncic plenty of times in the game, leading to a few heated moments during the second quarter. Lendeborg got a technical foul following an exchange between the two players, only further heating up their matchup. Doncic ultimately got the last laugh, as he finished the game with 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists and hit a half-court shot in Lendeborg's face to close out the first half.

After the game, though, the 24-year-old rookie had some words for Doncic.

"A lot of flopping, a lot of foul baiting, a lot of playing to the ref, interesting first game for sure," Lendeborg said . "I had a lot of respect for him… But being in there firsthand, just watching all the whining, the complaining, I lost all respect. That was awful. Me getting frustrated, it isn't about the foul being called, it's about him complaining the entire game.

"…He sucks, he can't score on me. I said it the whole game."

Doncic attempted six field goals while Lendeborg guarded him and only scored one of them, but his stat line speaks for itself.

How Has the Sports World Reacted to Luka Doncic and Yaxel Lendeborg's Beef?

Despite Doncic's impressive performance on Wednesday, several personalities in the sports world have taken the rookie's side in the matter.

Podcaster and Warriors forward Draymond Green obviously came to the aid of his teammate, defending his actions throughout the game.

"Everybody's gonna be like 'He shouldn't talk to Luka, you shouldn't talk to Luka,' and I disagree with that s— 1000%," Green said . "You go talk to somebody, you talk until you can't talk no more. If he busts your a—, guess what, you play him again three more times and you go back at his a— again. …In this league everybody always be like 'certain guys you gotta respect.' I didn't come in this league like that. You earn respect."

It wasn't just his teammates, though, as media personality Stephen A. Smith took the rookie's side on the matter as well.

"I don't agree with WHAT Lendeborg said, because Luka Doncic does not suck," Smith said . "In that regard, no. I don't agree with him. But I do agree with him going after Luka the way that he did, competing the way that he competed, talking his talk and what have you.

"…Here's why I'm supportive in what Yaxel Lendeborg is saying. He's saying 'if you're so great, quit whining to the officials. Just go out there and bust my a—. But stop whining to the officials looking to them for help.' I was really ticked off when that ref gave Yaxel the technical foul in the second quarter. I'm calling out the NBA. NBA gotta stop that nonsense! Let them talk!"

The Lakers and Warriors are sure to have some heated matchups all season long after Wednesday's series opener, and all eyes will be on Doncic and Lendeborg whenever those games come around. The two teams are already closing in on another matchup, as they'll face each other once again Friday, October. 30 at 7:00 p.m. PT.

articles.title: Ken Carman rips Cavs over TV deal: ‘It’s bad for the fanbase’
articles.summary: NBA teams have been forced to go their own way with local television and streaming deals for the 2026-2027 season after the RSN ecosystem collapsed. And whil...
articles.body:
NBA teams have been forced to go their own way with local television and streaming deals for the 2026-2027 season after the RSN ecosystem collapsed. And while some teams have valued reach and accessibility, the Cleveland Cavaliers are not one of them.

Coming off an Eastern Conference Finals appearance, the Cavs were one of several teams to link up with streaming platform DAZN for games this season . However, with no linear channel to watch games and a DAZN season pass that costs more than the entire League Pass package, the Cavs are the least accessible team to watch in the NBA for local fans.

The situation has left the Cavaliers fanbase upset. On 92.3 The Fan, host Ken Carman voiced that frustration, saying many fans will opt out of following the team instead of paying for yet another exclusive streaming package.

"Take the temperature of the fan base. I think a lot of fans are just down on them, the way the season ended last year, they didn't get LeBron. Listen, LeBron has probably two years left, he's going to be load management. I do not pick the Sixers to go to the Finals this year. Can't say I pick us," Carman said.

"I think that so many people are down on them, they got to figure out a way to fix this and get this accessible to their fans. I think a lot of people are not going to pay this. It's bad for me, it's bad for the team, it's bad for the fanbase, it's bad for what we do. How am I supposed to sit here and talk about the Cavs? I got to pay it. I'll watch it. But how am I supposed to sit here and talk about the Cavs when nobody's going to watch them?"

The NBA is making preparations to launch its own centralized hub for local broadcasts , which could be ready by next season. For Cavs fans and others with accessibility issues, it can't come soon enough.
